newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Chevron says sales near for PNG gas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Chevron says sales near for PNG gas pipeline.

text.p: South Pacific Chevron Co, a unit of Chevron Corp, said on Tuesday that a proposed A$3 billion gas pipeline from Papua New Guinea to the Australian state of Queensland is close to reaching sales agreements.

John Powell, project manager for the 2,400 km pipeline, said talks were in advanced stages with industrial gas consumers in the port cities of Townsville and Gladstone over taking gas starting in around mid-2001. "We hope to have memorandums of understanding by the middle of the year," Powell told reporters.
Chevron has been designated operator of the project, which includes as a partner the Papua New Guinea government.
Powell said the project would need to secure minimum sales contracts of about 200 million cubic feet a day of gas -- a third of total capacity -- to justify constructing the pipeline.

Papua New Guinea would seek to take up its full entitlement of 22.5 percent in the pipeline under its existing foreign ownership rules, Bernard Pawih, assistant director of the Papua New Guinea Department of Mining and Petroleum, told reporters.
The final ownership structure of the pipeline has not been resolved yet, although potential partners included those within and outside the Kutubu operation, Powell said.
South Pacific Chevron is proposing to deliver gas from the Kutubu gas field in the Southern Highlands of Papua New Guinea to Queenland via Torres Strait.
Chevron operates the Kutubu field. Together with other property held by South Pacific Chevron, total gas reserves were between eight and nine trillion cubic feet, Powell said.
Powell said the Townsville and Gladstone regions offered growth potential for gas sales, given exisiting and proposed industrial projects in the areas.
The project will initially target only large consumers of gas, he said.
MIM Holdings Ltd operates a copper refinery in Townsville, which is expanding its capacity to 250,000 tonnes a year from the current 175,000 tonnes.
Near Gladstone, Comalco Ltd operates the Boyne Island aluminium smelter, which is installing a third potline boost production.
Also, Korea Zinc Co Ltd has proposed builing a A$1 billion zinc smelter in Townsville.
Powell said the Queensland government was likely to favour future development of gas-fired power stations over coal-fired ones because on environmental grounds.
The possibility existed to constructing a liquefied natural gas production plant as part of the project, although this was some years off, Powell added.
